scope: Native OpenAI enrichment batches and durable recovery; not full M4 acceptance
checks: Native OpenAI chat/embedding binding adds the pinned SDK batch lifecycle; explicit model batch capability and shared privacy transport remain required.
At most sixteen automatic enrichment jobs form one active batch. Manual enrichment stays interactive. Shared budget reservation and job ownership commit atomically before upload.
Upload and submission intents, remote ids, result payloads and item progress persist separately. Ambiguous responses reconcile without blind resubmission.
Startup preserves active batch leases and unsettled reservations. Existing non-batch recovery behavior is retained.
Publication checks the current document, source, credential, configuration and lease; cancellation and purge cannot publish stale results.
Known per-item usage settles once; missing or invalid totals retain the reservation. Partial, unordered and missing results have explicit outcomes.
Native response sizes, JSONL lines, line lengths, item counts and ids are bounded. Redirects, raw errors, unsafe paths and unsupported declarations fail closed.
Collected results recover after publication interruption. Terminal batches release local payload references for retention; remote input/output deletion follows collection or cancellation.
The schema-seven to schema-eight transition requires a complete encrypted pre-upgrade backup. Portable export includes non-content batch metadata.
Desktop and phone settings checks save and reload the backfill preference without overflow; screenshots were reviewed.
packageAdvisories: NuGet listed no known vulnerabilities for this restored graph at this check
limitations: Native Anthropic batching and verified span-level citation integration remain unfinished.
No live OpenAI account or cloud model was called; protocol checks use controlled HTTP responses and storage tests use a controlled batch provider.
Unconfirmed uploads/submissions are not retried blindly. After bounded reconciliation windows the job fails conservatively and retains audit metadata.
Changed provider endpoints or refused remote deletion retain ids and a cleanup-pending reason for operator follow-up; the application does not send saved ids to a different endpoint.
Full sustained-write daemon restore, mounted/large-corpus, hardened deployment, signed-release and remaining real-export acceptance are open.
